# Mixed column/page anchors in table cells

Original XML controls generated by `tools/mixed_cell_anchor_fixture.py` from the
repository's original table-global-anchor fixtures. Four pages cross behind/in
front with layoutInCell true/false. Each drawing is in the second cell, with a
10pt column-relative horizontal offset and a 12pt page-relative vertical offset.
The two packages use compatibility modes 15 and 12. No corpus artwork is included.

The reference application exported the PDFs; all eight native pages were visually
inspected. `reference.json` records native image bounds in points, top-left
page coordinates, extracted from PDF page objects. Every image is 72 by 36pt:

- Mode 15: every frame is at (226, 86), regardless of layoutInCell.
- Mode 12 with layoutInCell=true: frames are also at (226, 86).
- Mode 12 with layoutInCell=false: frames are at (82, 12).
- Behind-text drawings are covered by the cell shading when located in the cell;
  their image objects remain in the PDF. Do not infer frame absence from paint.

Both packages pass the supported schema checks. An initial generator property
ordering error was corrected before these native references were recaptured.
`hashes.json` identifies source and native artifacts. Unit coverage checks all
eight frames, pagination, hit testing and editing/package preservation. Browser
coverage compares native blue drawing masks and checks editing, export, undo
and reopening. The implementation supports numeric column/page wrapNone anchors.

This extends the coordinate family represented by `table-global-anchors`, whose
README records the existing compatibility-mode/layoutInCell divergence from the
literal ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.4.2.3 description. No new divergence is claimed from
these four offset cases alone; other mixed axes and wrapping modes need evidence.
